milestone: STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P5C -- disk growth measurement (Part 8) and steady-state model (Part 12)
observation_window_note: Extremely short window (~35 minutes). All growth figures below are PRELIMINARY and explicitly labeled OBSERVED (real, measured) vs MODELED (extrapolated/theoretical) per the milestone's Part 12 instruction.

sizes_at_cutover.cold_segments_total_bytes: not separately recorded at cutover in prior artifacts; current value used as the only available reference point

sizes_now_OBSERVED.evidence_platform_note: du -sh database/evidence_platform reported alongside intelligence_snapshots in a combined background call; evidence_platform measured at same pass as logs/intelligence_snapshots below.

growth_since_cutover_OBSERVED.cold_growth_note: COLD segment count (45) and total manifest row count (1,746,519) are IDENTICAL to the cutover baseline -- zero COLD growth since cutover. This is expected: Part 10 confirms no automated HOT->COLD rollover exists post-cutover, so COLD is currently static.

projection_PRELIMINARY_MODELED.basis: Linear extrapolation of the observed ~35-minute HOT byte growth rate (172,173,681 bytes/hour). Explicitly flagged low-confidence given the short window; post-restart traffic may not be representative of steady state.
projection_PRELIMINARY_MODELED.caveat: A 30-day projection of ~124 GiB growth from a 35-minute sample, if taken literally, would exceed current free disk (37 GiB) well before 30 days -- this is exactly why the milestone brief requires this figure to be clearly labeled preliminary rather than presented as a confident forecast. The Part 12 steady-state model below (based on the previously qualified ~172k rows/day long-run average, not this 35-minute sample) is the more credible planning reference; the two should be read together, not the short-sample figure alone.

observed_this_session.directional_consistency_with_model: The observed id-based rate (79,359 rows/hour -> ~1,904,615 rows/day projected) is roughly 11x higher than the established long-run model average of ~172,000 rows/day (~7,167 rows/hour). This is NOT interpreted as a contradiction of the model -- a 35-minute sample immediately following a service restart is expected to be noisy and potentially inflated by backfill/catch-up traffic following the ~6-minute writer downtime during cutover. The count-based rate (54,629 rows/hour) is closer but still elevated. Neither observed rate should be used to revise the long-run model; both are flagged as directionally uninformative at this sample size and should be re-measured after the full 24-72h observation window.

MODELED_established_baseline.modeled_steady_state_hot_row_count: raw_ingestion_rate * 90-day generic window + permanently-pinned accumulation beyond the window; using 172,000/day * 90 = 15,480,000 generic-window rows, plus pinned rows accumulating indefinitely on top -- exact steady-state row count depends on how long the system has already been running the 90-day policy, which requires the HOT->COLD automation (Part 10) to actually exist and run before a true steady state can be reached or measured
MODELED_established_baseline.modeled_steady_state_hot_db_size_note: Not independently re-derived in this review beyond the existing P5B baseline sizing (~13.8GB HOT at 3,647,480 rows at cutover implies roughly ~3.8KB/row average including index/page overhead); a precise steady-state byte estimate would require this per-row byte figure applied to the modeled steady-state row count above, but since HOT->COLD rollover is NOT currently automated (Part 10), HOT will NOT reach the modeled 90-day-windowed steady state on its own -- it will instead grow UNBOUNDED at the raw ingestion rate until automation exists, which is the central finding driving Part 15's automation-gap policy.

part12_hot_steady_state_model.verdict: OBSERVED short-window rates are noisy/elevated and not treated as model-invalidating. MODELED steady-state figures remain the reference baseline, but are currently ASPIRATIONAL rather than descriptive of live HOT behavior, because HOT->COLD automation does not yet exist to bound HOT to the 90-day window (see automation census artifact).
